---
title: "8.4 Assumptions"
order: 4
---

Six assumptions carry the output. For each: what it is, the evidence, and what breaks if it
fails.

## The increase is drawn at today's utilisation {#li-drawdown}

**The assumption.** An increase is not a loan: the bank commits a higher limit and the
customer draws some of it. `incremental_exposure` assumes the new headroom is drawn at the
account's current on-book utilisation, so the incremental EAD is the increase times that
utilisation ([8.3](methodology.qmd#li-roe)). Every dollar figure the module reports — the
incremental exposure, the incremental net income, `segments`' exposure by band — rests on it.

**The evidence.** Three parts, two of them exact:

- **Per loan, the ROE does not depend on it.** Every line of `profit_waterfall` is
  proportional to EAD, so the ROE of an increase is the same whatever share of it is drawn:
  across the offers, the ROE at the incremental EAD and at an EAD of one differ by
  {{< var li.econ.ead_invariance >}}. `line_increase/docs/validation_report.md` states this,
  and it is right per loan. No account's verdict moves with the drawdown.
- **The aggregate depends on it, slightly.** The gate tests the offers' aggregate ROE, total
  net income over total allocated equity: an equity-weighted mean of the per-loan ROEs, with
  weights set by each offer's EAD. Scaling every offer's EAD by the same factor leaves it
  unchanged — re-priced offer by offer at half its EAD, it moves by
  {{< var li.econ.agg_uniform_invariance >}} — but changing their relative sizes moves it. If
  every increase were fully drawn, the same {{< var li.econ.full_draw.n_offered >}} accounts
  would be offered and the aggregate would be {{< var li.econ.full_draw.agg_roe >}} instead
  of {{< var li.agg_roe >}}.
- **The exposure depends on it entirely.** The {{< var li.n_offered >}} offers commit
  \${{< var li.econ.amount_total >}} of new limit; the assumed drawn exposure is
  \${{< var li.econ.exposure_total >}} ([8.5](performance.qmd#li-economics)). Nothing in the
  data says how much of an increase a business draws; the generator never grants one.

The assumption **holds for the verdicts and not for the dollars**: who is offered does not
depend on it, how much exposure the offers add does, and that figure is unvalidated —
finding 5 ([8.7](limitations.qmd)).

**What breaks if it fails.** A business offered more room because it is near its limit may
well draw more than its current share of the new room. Exposure, capital and income would
then all be higher than reported, by up to the committed amount. The ROE verdicts would not
change.

## The caps and `target_util` are policy, not estimates {#li-caps}

**The assumption.** `target_util`, `pct_cap`, `revenue_mult_cap` and `round_to` in
`shared.config.LINE_INCREASE` are credit policy: a utilisation the bank is comfortable with
after an increase, a largest single step, and a ceiling against revenue. None is fitted, and
the assumption is that each is a sensible limit for this book.

**The evidence.** Each binds on some accounts ([8.3](methodology.qmd#li-amount)): among the
offers, headroom to target utilisation binds on {{< var li.caps.headroom_to_target_util.offers >}},
the revenue ceiling on {{< var li.caps.revenue_ceiling.offers >}} and the share of the limit
on {{< var li.caps.pct_cap.offers >}}. `target_util` does more than size the increase: an
amount exists only above it, so it decides who can be offered anything, and moving it by
{{< var li.sens.step >}} moves the offers from {{< var li.n_offered >}} to between
{{< var li.sens.target_util.up.n_offered >}} and {{< var li.sens.target_util.down.n_offered >}}
([8.6](sensitivity.qmd)). No document records who set the values or why. The assumption
**holds as policy**: the values do what the code says and none is dead, but none is
justified by evidence about the book.

**What breaks if it fails.** A `target_util` set too low offers more room to accounts that
are not constrained; too high, and the offers dry up. Changing any of them changes the
offers without a retrain, and the cohort gates would not notice (finding 1).

## The threshold and the ceiling are fixed shares {#li-shares}

**The assumption.** The offer threshold and the PD ceiling are not levels the bank chose; they
are the {{< var li.config.offer_quantile >}} quantile of the model's probability and the
{{< var li.config.max_pd_quantile >}} quantile of the scorecard's PD, both over the whole
book, re-taken on every retrain ([8.3](methodology.qmd#li-threshold)). The assumption is that
a fixed share of the book is the right appetite.

**The evidence.** On this book the threshold is {{< var li.offer_threshold >}} and the
ceiling {{< var li.offer_max_pd >}}. The threshold is taken partly over in-sample
probabilities; on accounts the model has not seen it lets through
{{< var li.thr.share_holdout >}}, close to the {{< var li.thr.share_book >}} intended, and
its held-out observed rate among the accounts above it, {{< var li.thr_ho.observed >}}
against a mean probability of {{< var li.thr_ho.predicted >}}, is
{{< var li.thr_ho.status >}} ([8.5](performance.qmd#li-cohort)). The assumption **holds in
part**: the mechanics behave on new accounts, but the PD ceiling is relative, so a retrain on
a riskier book would raise it and keep offering to half the book.

**What breaks if it fails.** The ceiling is called a risk appetite, but it moves with the
book. A deteriorating book would keep its offer rate and accept a higher PD; the monitoring
plan watches the ceiling itself on every retrain ([8.8](monitoring.qmd)).

## The score is a valid input {#li-the-score}

**The assumption.** `pd_score` comes from the saved scorecard ([8.2](data.qmd#li-score-input))
and is what D4 documents: a valid ranking of credit risk.

**The evidence.** It is computed by `predict_score_pd`, never from the generator's truth. It
is in-sample for the scorecard on most booked accounts. And it carries D4's findings into
three places at once — the model, the ceiling and the price. One matters directly: on the
held-out booked, band B under-predicts (D4 finding 6), and band B receives the most offers,
{{< var li.band.B.offers >}} of {{< var li.n_offered >}} ([8.5](performance.qmd#li-bands)).
The assumption **holds**, with the dependency stated.

**What breaks if it fails.** A scorecard change moves the ceiling, the model's input and every
increment's ROE: retrain, re-take both quantiles and re-assert the gate
([D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd#what-a-scorecard-change-forces)).

## The label means "a good candidate" {#li-the-label}

**The assumption.** `{{< var li.target >}}` marks the accounts to which an increase would
have been good for the bank, so ranking by it ranks candidates.

**The evidence.** The generator draws it from the true PD, utilisation above a level,
revenue and, with a small weight, later deterioration ([8.2](data.qmd#li-label)). It is drawn
for every account, though no account was ever offered an increase; there is no record of an
offer, a take-up, a drawdown or a repayment. The label is a construction of the generator, not
an outcome of an increase. The assumption **holds only by definition** — finding 6.

**What breaks if it fails.** On a real book the outcome of an increase exists only for
accounts that were given one, chosen by an earlier policy. A model trained on those alone
learns that policy's choices as well as the outcome; one trained on a constructed label, as
here, learns the construction.

## The generator as ground truth

**The assumption.** As in D4 (D4.4): every label in the data was drawn by
`shared/data_generator.py`, and every claim in this chapter is a statement about that
generator ([D1](../d1-purpose.qmd#scope-synthetic-data-real-methods)).

**The evidence.** The generator is code, which is how this chapter can state the ceiling on
ranking ([8.5](performance.qmd#li-ceiling)) and say that the label is constructed rather than
observed.

**What breaks if it fails.** On real data the label would need a definition and an
observation window, the drawdown would be measured rather than assumed, and the caps would
meet distributions no one has looked at. Each is named above or in [8.7](limitations.qmd).
